title: Uniform compact model for a small diagram of right adjoints
statement: Use universes, infinite regular cardinals, compactness and presentability from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and coherent infinity categories, functors, spaces and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Small means in the smaller universe; $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ here contains categories small in a containing universe, so its objects may be large in the smaller universe. Let $A$ be a small infinity category and $H:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ a coherent diagram whose values are presentable infinity categories and whose arrows are right adjoints. There is an uncountable infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$ in the smaller universe for which every $H(a)$ is $\lambda$-accessible and every arrow of $H$ preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. There is a coherent functor $F_0:A\to\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda)}_\infty$, where the target consists of small infinity categories admitting $\lambda$-small colimits and functors preserving these colimits. For a small infinity category $C$, define $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)$ to be the full subcategory of $\mathcal P(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ spanned by small $\lambda$-filtered colimits of representable presheaves, with $\mathcal S$ the category of small spaces. For small infinity categories $C,D$ admitting $\lambda$-small colimits and a functor $u:C\to D$ preserving those colimits, the $\lambda$-filtered-colimit-preserving extension of $u$ along Yoneda is a left adjoint $u_!:\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)\to\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(D)$; denote its right adjoint by $u^*$. These constructions define a coherent contravariant functor $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda^{\mathrm R}$ on $\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda)}_\infty$. There is a natural equivalence $H\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda^{\mathrm R}\circ F_0^{\mathrm{op}}$: at $a$ it identifies $H(a)$ with $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(F_0(a))$, and for $f:a\to a'$ it identifies $H(f^{\mathrm{op}})$ with the right adjoint of $(F_0(f))_!$. Each $F_0(a)$ may be chosen equivalent to the full subcategory of $\lambda$-compact objects of $H(a)$. The equivalence is one of coherent diagrams, including all higher simplices. Here $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is left adjoint to $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ when there is an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Lx,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,Ry)$ natural coherently in $x,y$, with the corresponding coherent unit and counit satisfying the triangle identities.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 10.3, final paragraph (uniform lambda and compact-object diagram); Definition 10.4. Higher Topos Theory Proposition 5.5.7.2, Notation 5.5.7.7 and Propositions 5.5.7.8-5.5.7.10 give the compact-object/Ind equivalence; GHN supplies the simultaneous cardinal choice for a small diagram. Read online; archival copies WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: For each arrow f:a→a′ of A, the functor H(fᵒᵖ):H(a′)→H(a) is a coherent right adjoint between presentable infinity categories. By the accessibility theorem for right adjoints, choose a regular cardinal ρ_f for which it preserves small ρ_f-filtered colimits.

The objects H(a) and arrows H(fᵒᵖ) form a small family. Applying the common-rank lemma to this family and the ranks ρ_f gives one uncountable infinite regular λ for which every H(a) is λ-accessible and every arrow preserves small λ-filtered colimits.

By step 2, H factors through Pr^{R,λ}_∞: its values are presentable and λ-accessible and its arrows admit left adjoints and preserve small λ-filtered colimits. Apply compact-object/Ind duality at the uncountable λ. Clause (2) turns H into a coherent functor A→Pr^{L,λ}_∞ with the same values, carrying f to a left adjoint of H(fᵒᵖ), which preserves λ-compact objects by clause (1). Composing with the quasi-inverse in clause (3) gives a coherent functor F₀:A→Cat^rex(λ)_∞ whose value F₀(a) is a small model of the full λ-compact subcategory of H(a), and whose arrow F₀(f) is the restriction of the left adjoint of H(fᵒᵖ). The same equivalences identify H(a) with Ind_λ(F₀(a)) and H(fᵒᵖ) with the right adjoint of the Ind extension of F₀(f), coherently in f and in all higher simplices.

For each small F₀(a), the notation Ind_λ(F₀(a)) means the full subcategory of Fun(F₀(a)ᵒᵖ,S) spanned by small λ-filtered colimits of representables; since F₀(a) admits λ-small colimits, Ind_λ(F₀(a)) is presentable and the Yoneda embedding preserves λ-small colimits (lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability). The filtered-completion theorem (lem-coef-ind-kappa-extension) gives the essentially unique λ-filtered-colimit-preserving extension u_! of j∘u for each arrow u=F₀(f), with its coherent transformation data, and its last clause shows that u_! preserves all small colimits because u preserves λ-small colimits and the target is presentable. By the adjoint functor theorem (lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints) u_! has a right adjoint u^*, so u_! is a left adjoint as the statement asserts.

By clause (3) of the duality node, Ind_λ on Cat^rex(λ)_∞ sends u to the extension u_! of step 4, so composing it with the equivalence of clause (2) gives the coherent contravariant functor Ind^R_λ:C↦Ind_λ(C), u↦u^*. Since Ind_λ is quasi-inverse to the compact-object functor used in step 3, the objectwise identifications of step 3 assemble to a natural equivalence of coherent diagrams H≃Ind^R_λ∘F₀ᵒᵖ, including all higher simplices. The final mapping-space characterization of a left/right adjunction is the stated coherent unit-counit condition.
